name: Conventional Deadlift
summary: A full-body pull from the floor that trains the glutes, hamstrings, back and grip. It is one of the best exercises for overall strength when done with good technique.
setup: Stand with your feet about hip width apart and the bar over your midfoot, close to your shins.
Hinge and bend your knees to grip the bar just outside your legs with straight arms.
Pull the slack out of the bar, set your lats by pulling the bar into your body, and bring your chest up.
Take a big breath, brace your trunk and keep a neutral spine.
execution: Push the floor away with your legs while keeping the bar close to your body.
Keep your back angle the same until the bar passes your knees.
Drive your hips forward and stand tall, squeezing your glutes at the top without leaning back.
Lower by pushing your hips back first, then bending the knees once the bar passes them.
Reset your setup and breath before every rep.
mistakes: Rounding the lower back: lower the weight and focus on bracing and setting the lats before pulling.
Bar drifting forward away from the body: start with the bar over the midfoot and keep your lats engaged.
Hips shooting up first: think about pushing the floor away rather than pulling with the back.
Leaning back or hyperextending at lockout: finish tall by squeezing the glutes, not by arching.

references.title: Build A Bigger Deadlift With Perfect Technique (Conventional Form)
references.author: Jeff Nippard
